sources.title: Praxis: relutrigine NDA acceptance
sources.summary: Praxis reported acceptance of the relutrigine NDA with priority review for SCN2A and SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies; the original target was September 27, 2026. The submission uses EMBOLD data.

sources.title: Praxis: relutrigine three-month extension
sources.summary: Praxis reported that additional sensitivity analyses of existing clinical data were a major amendment; the target moved from September 27 to December 27, 2026. The company said no new study was requested and the notice cited no safety or manufacturing concerns.
sources.excerpt: FDA sets updated PDUFA date of December 27, 2026

sources.title: Praxis: August regulatory update filed with SEC
sources.summary: Praxis reported a completed relutrigine mid-cycle meeting without major safety or efficacy concerns identified to date or a planned advisory committee. It reported BIMO sponsor inspections for relutrigine and ulixacaltamide ended without a Form 483. This is sponsor-reported clinical-research oversight, not manufacturing-site clearance. Praxis said it would not communicate further regulatory updates before the expected targets.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: EMBOLD
sources.summary: The current registry describes a randomized, masked phase 2/3 study of PRAX-562 (relutrigine), including monthly motor-seizure frequency and longer-term safety assessments. Estimated enrollment is 77 across cohorts; this is not the efficacy analysis sample size. Primary completion is recorded as November 12, 2025; no registry results are posted.

sources.title: Scholar Rock: apitegromab complete response
sources.summary: Scholar Rock reported a complete response letter tied to observations from an inspection at Catalent Indiana, its third-party fill-finish site. This historical setback belongs to apitegromab, not a general company-wide risk assumption.

sources.title: Scholar Rock: second fill-finish facility pathway
sources.summary: Scholar Rock reported Catalent Indiana received an OAI inspection classification. It will remove that site from the apitegromab BLA under FDA guidance. Review proceeds with a second facility and the September 30 target remains. The sponsor says the alternative site package was submitted and commercial vials are available.
sources.excerpt: FDA review of second fill-finish facility progressing

sources.title: FDA: Catalent Indiana inspection observations
sources.summary: FDA Form 483 issued April 24, 2026 after an April 13–24 inspection at Catalent Indiana, Bloomington, FEI 3005949964. Observations include investigation, visual-inspection, aseptic-process and sampling controls. Product details are redacted. The document does not establish that observations concern apitegromab lots, and a Form 483 is not a final agency determination. Exact public posting date was not established.

sources.title: Scholar Rock: SAPPHIRE clinical results
sources.summary: The sponsor reported a 1.8-point HFMSE difference at week 52 for combined apitegromab doses versus placebo, both with standard care (p=0.0192). The 20 mg/kg group alone had a 1.4-point difference (p=0.1149). The distinction between the prespecified combined analysis and individual doses matters.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: SAPPHIRE
sources.summary: The registry describes a randomized, masked phase 3 trial in later-onset SMA on nusinersen or risdiplam, with actual enrollment of 188. The main efficacy outcome is HFMSE total-score change. Primary completion was December 18, 2024. No results are currently posted in the registry.

sources.title: Ultragenyx: UX111 prior complete response
sources.summary: Ultragenyx reported a CRL requesting CMC improvements and information associated with manufacturing inspection observations. It characterized clinical data as robust and biomarker evidence as supportive, attributing those views to FDA reviews.

sources.title: Ultragenyx: UX111 resubmission accepted
sources.summary: Ultragenyx reported FDA acceptance of its resubmitted BLA seeking accelerated approval of UX111 for MPS IIIA, with September 19, 2026 as the action target. The submission includes longer follow-up; final adequacy of the package and manufacturing review is not public.
sources.excerpt: PDUFA action date set for September 19, 2026

sources.title: Ultragenyx: Q2 2026 regulatory update
sources.summary: The second-quarter update continued to list the accepted resubmitted UX111 BLA and September 19, 2026 action target. The separate DTX401 program must not be mistaken for UX111.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: UX111 gene-transfer trial
sources.summary: The registry links UX111 to ABO-102 and rebisufligene etisparvovec. It describes a nonrandomized, open-label gene-transfer trial, estimated enrollment 36, with CSF heparan-sulfate exposure as a primary measure. No registry results are posted. The planned total enrollment is not the application efficacy population.

sources.title: Capricor: deramiocel extension and refined indication
sources.summary: Capricor reported the target moved from August 22 to November 22, 2026. After a July advisory committee, it submitted 24-month HOPE-3 open-label follow-up and robustness analyses, seeking an indication focused on upper-limb function. FDA accepted the material as a major amendment. The sponsor reports HOPE-3 met its primary endpoint.

sources.title: FDA: deramiocel July 2026 advisory-committee briefing
sources.summary: FDA’s briefing for July 29, 2026 concerns resubmitted BLA 125842 and the then-proposed cardiomyopathy indication. Printed pages 32–34 describe the June 18, 2025 final visit, SAP 2.0 dated September 26, SAP 3.0 dated November 24, and database lock/unblinding November 25. Changes were post-completion, not necessarily post-unblinding; FDA questions raw-to-percent endpoint conversion. Appendix table 12, printed page 52 (PDF page 52), gives p=0.11 under SAP 1.1 versus p=0.045 under SAP 3.0; sensitivity analyses differ. Printed page 47 gives the unfavorable pre-meeting effectiveness assessment. This precedes the sponsor’s August refined-indication amendment; it is not a final decision on that amendment. Exact posting day was not established.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: HOPE-3
sources.summary: HOPE-3 is a randomized, masked phase 3 study of deramiocel (CAP-1002) in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The registry reports actual enrollment of 106 and primary completion June 18, 2025. The primary measure is upper-limb function at month 12; an open-label extension follows the blinded period. No registry results are posted.

sources.title: Summit: ivonescimab BLA accepted
sources.summary: Summit reported its ivonescimab-plus-chemotherapy BLA was accepted for EGFR-mutated non-squamous NSCLC after TKI treatment, with November 14, 2026 as the action target. The filing is based on the global HARMONi trial, not HARMONi-2 or HARMONi-6.

sources.title: Summit: HARMONi primary analysis and upcoming update
sources.summary: Summit reported median PFS of 6.8 versus 4.4 months (HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.41–0.66; p<0.0001). Primary OS analysis did not reach significance. It said updated OS detail would be presented September 15; those future details are outside this catalog cutoff. The November 14 action target was reaffirmed.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: global HARMONi
sources.summary: The global randomized, masked phase 3 HARMONi study enrolled 420 patients. PFS and overall survival are primary outcomes; primary completion is April 12, 2025. The population has EGFR-mutated non-squamous NSCLC progressing after EGFR-TKI therapy. No registry results are posted.

sources.title: Savara: molgramostim major-amendment extension
sources.summary: Savara reported responses to FDA information requests were a major amendment and the priority-review target was extended three months to November 22, 2026. It said the correspondence cited no safety, efficacy or manufacturing concerns.

sources.title: Savara: Q2 2026 review status
sources.summary: Savara reaffirmed November 22, 2026 as the molgramostim BLA target. It described long-term lung-function and respiratory-quality-of-life improvement and stated MOLBREEVI is a proposed brand, not an approved medicine.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: IMPALA-2
sources.summary: The registry describes a randomized, masked phase 3 trial of inhaled molgramostim versus placebo, with 164 enrolled. Its primary measure is hemoglobin-adjusted percent-predicted DLCO change at week 24. Primary completion was November 30, 2023 and results are posted.

sources.title: Nuvalent: neladalkib priority-review acceptance
sources.summary: Nuvalent announced priority-review acceptance for neladalkib in TKI-pretreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC, with a November 27, 2026 target. The application uses ALKOVE-1 phase 1/2 data; the registrational phase 2 portion is single-arm and open-label.

sources.title: GSK: completed Nuvalent acquisition
sources.summary: GSK announced completion of its acquisition of Nuvalent. Neladalkib was still under FDA review; the sponsor identity here reflects the completed acquisition rather than obsolete standalone-company information.

sources.title: GSK: Q2 2026 portfolio update
sources.summary: GSK’s Q2 update distinguished FDA-approved Jideytro (zidesamtinib) from neladalkib, which still had a forthcoming FDA target. The two acquired kinase inhibitors have different targets and review outcomes.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: ALKOVE-1
sources.summary: The phase 1/2 registry describes a nonrandomized, open-label study of neladalkib (NVL-655), including phase 2 response rate by independent review. Estimated enrollment 840 covers the wider protocol, not just the submitted efficacy group. No registry results are posted.

sources.title: PolyPid: completed D-PLEX100 NDA submission
sources.summary: PolyPid announced its completed rolling NDA for prevention of surgical-site infection after colorectal surgery. At that time it anticipated an action in Q1 2027; this was guidance, not an assigned target.

sources.title: PolyPid: priority-review acceptance and updated target
sources.summary: PolyPid reported FDA accepted D-PLEX100 on July 27 with priority review and November 28, 2026 as the target. It reported SHIELD II met primary and key secondary endpoints and a 60% relative SSI reduction (p=0.0013). It said filing communications identified no issues; full substantive review remained ahead.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov: SHIELD II
sources.summary: The randomized, masked phase 3 study enrolled 975. Its primary analysis uses a composite of SSI, re-intervention or death within 30 days in subjects with target incisions over 20 cm. This is not identical to SSI alone across all surgeries. Primary completion was April 14, 2025 and results are posted.

sources.title: Telix: Pixclara NDA resubmission accepted
sources.summary: Telix reported acceptance of its resubmitted NDA for TLX101-Px (floretyrosine F 18; proposed Pixclara brand), an investigational PET agent for glioma imaging, with a September 11, 2026 target. The indication distinguishes recurrent or progressive glioma from treatment-related change. Resubmission occurred March 13.

sources.title: Telix: half-year 2026 pipeline status
sources.summary: Telix reaffirmed September 11, 2026 as the Pixclara action target. TLX101-Px is the imaging candidate; TLX101-Tx is a different therapeutic candidate and Zircaix is a separate kidney-imaging application.

coverage.title: Nine real FDA review episodes
coverage.description: Manually curated and source-linked public evidence for nine drug–indication or diagnostic review episodes, checked September 10, 2026. This is a focused demonstration collection, not a census or model-training cohort.
limitations: Current review status reflects the latest identified sponsor/SEC disclosures and a contemporaneous outcome search; FDA does not publish a complete live pending-application registry.
All FDA action dates are sponsor-reported targets. They are not approval predictions, and may change or precede an earlier action.
No numerical approval probabilities are supplied by this catalog. Supportive/concern labels are qualitative curation, not a trained score or Astra output.
Sponsor statements and SEC-filed sponsor exhibits are attributed reports, not independent FDA conclusions. Trial registry records are submitted by responsible parties.
Trial snapshots are current at retrieval. Do not use later-updated records as historical features without a historical version; total enrollment may differ from a pivotal analysis population.
Missing manufacturing findings, unpublished results and unobserved regulatory correspondence are unknown, not evidence that a concern is absent.
The Catalent Form 483 issue date is known but its exact public posting date is not. It must be excluded from historical as-of backtests unless first-public availability is established.
No private FDAgent data, customer uploads or fictional company records are included. Source summaries are human/agent-curated; new Astra investigations carry separate provenance.
